title: The Information Geometry of Representation Formation
abstract: arXiv:2610.34015v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Most analyses of neural representations focus on trained endpoints, leaving the process by which internal structure forms comparatively unmeasured. We instead treat representation formation itself as an object of study, asking whether the path a representation takes through training reveals information that its endpoint does not. We formalize this idea by viewing representation learning as a geometric trajectory, using Bures geometry to measure movement through representation space and quantum Fisher information to characterize local sensitivity to input factors. We find that learning concentrates local sensitivity on task-relevant factors, and that changing only the prediction target reorganizes this geometry around the corresponding visual factor. More strikingly, representation trajectories become systematically less direct as the learned computation requires higher-order interactions among input factors. This effect persists under

translated_abstract: 大多数对神经表征的分析都聚焦于训练完成后的最终状态，而内部结构形成的过程却相对缺乏测量。我们转而将表征形成过程本身作为研究对象，探究表征在训练中所走的路径是否揭示了其终点无法提供的信息。我们通过将表征学习视为一条几何轨迹来形式化这一想法，利用Bures几何来度量在表征空间中的移动，并用量子Fisher信息来刻画对输入因素的局部敏感性。我们发现，学习会使局部敏感性集中于与任务相关的因素，并且仅改变预测目标就会使这种几何结构围绕相应的视觉因素进行重组。更引人注目的是，随着所学计算需要输入因素之间的高阶交互，表征轨迹会系统性地变得不那么直接。该效应在（原文摘要在此处截断）……条件下依然持续存在。
tldr: 该论文将表征形成过程本身作为研究对象，用Bures几何与量子Fisher信息刻画训练中表征的几何轨迹，发现学习会将局部敏感性集中于任务相关因素，且当所学计算需要更高阶的输入交互时，表征轨迹会系统性地变得更不直接。
en_tdlr: The paper treats representation formation itself as an object of study, formalizing it as a geometric trajectory using Bures geometry and quantum Fisher information, and finds that learning concentrates local sensitivity on task-relevant factors while trajectories become systematically less direct as the learned computation requires higher-order interactions among input factors.
